facts.fact: Baymard's large-scale usability testing found that 95% of users relied on reviews to evaluate products or learn about them.
facts.quote: 95% of users in Baymard’s large-scale usability testing relied on reviews to evaluate products or learn about them

facts.fact: Baymard reported that some users used review details instead of the merchant's description or specifications.
facts.quote: some used review details instead of the merchant’s description or specifications

facts.fact: Northwestern's Spiegel Research Center, using ecommerce data supplied by PowerReviews, found five reviews increased purchase likelihood by approximately 270% versus no reviews.
facts.unit: % relative increase in purchase likelihood vs no reviews
facts.quote: five reviews increased purchase likelihood by approximately 270% versus no reviews

facts.fact: Spiegel Research Center reported that five reviews lifted purchase likelihood by up to 380% for higher-priced products.
facts.unit: % relative increase in purchase likelihood vs no reviews
facts.quote: reported lifts reaching 380% for higher-priced products

facts.fact: Spiegel Research Center reported that five reviews lifted purchase likelihood by approximately 190% for lower-priced products.
facts.unit: % relative increase in purchase likelihood vs no reviews
facts.quote: approximately 190% for lower-priced products

facts.fact: The Spiegel lifts are relative changes in purchase likelihood from observational data, not promised percentage-point increases in conversion rate.
facts.quote: Those are relative changes in purchase likelihood from observational ecommerce data, not promised percentage-point increases in your conversion rate

facts.fact: The vendor recommends starting with five genuine reviews for expensive or hard-to-evaluate products.
facts.quote: Start with **five genuine reviews for expensive or hard-to-evaluate products**

facts.fact: For lower-priced products, the vendor's suggested first target is 2 to 4 reviews, then 5 if collection is easy.
facts.quote: Lower-priced | 2 to 4, then 5 if collection is easy

facts.fact: On one ecommerce site cited by SearchLab, nearly all the review-driven improvement occurred within the first 10 reviews.
facts.quote: nearly all the improvement occurred within the first **10 reviews**

facts.fact: SearchLab's summary says the first five reviews produced most of the gain on the cited ecommerce site.
facts.quote: with the first **five** producing most of the gain

facts.fact: According to the 2025 Salsify Ecommerce Pulse Report, 46% of consumers named knowing whether reviews are real or trustworthy as their top shopping-journey frustration.
facts.quote: 46% of consumers identified knowing whether reviews are real or trustworthy as their top shopping-journey frustration

facts.fact: According to the 2025 Salsify Ecommerce Pulse Report, ratings and reviews influenced final buying decisions 32% of the time.
facts.quote: ratings and reviews influenced final buying decisions **32% of the time**

facts.fact: A Dartmouth Tuck School working paper, as summarized by Buy with Prime, examined 380,450 product-page impressions involving more than 43,000 reviews in Technology and Home and Garden.
facts.quote: examined **380,450 product-page impressions** involving **more than 43,000 reviews** in Technology and Home and Garden

facts.fact: According to the Dartmouth Tuck School working paper as summarized by Buy with Prime, replacing a top-position one-star review with a five-star review increased purchase probability by 0.88 percentage points.
facts.quote: replacing a top-position one-star review with a five-star review increased purchase probability by **0.88 percentage points**

facts.fact: Google requires Product structured data to include at least one of the review, aggregateRating, or offers properties, according to Google's product snippet documentation.
facts.value: at least one of review, aggregateRating, or offers
facts.quote: Google requires Product structured data to include at least one of **`review`, `aggregateRating`, or `offers`**

facts.fact: Structured data for a product page does not guarantee that Google will display ratings.
facts.quote: structured data doesn’t guarantee that Google will display ratings

facts.fact: The guidance states that criticism remains published unless it violates a written content policy.
facts.quote: Explain that criticism remains unless it violates a written content policy.

facts.fact: The page advises keeping incentive disclosures visible in every version of a review test, and states that hiding a material disclosure is not an appropriate test condition.
facts.quote: Keep incentive disclosures visible in every version; hiding a material disclosure isn’t an appropriate test condition.

facts.fact: The page advises that empty review fields should never be turned into fabricated ratings when validating pages with and without reviews.
facts.quote: Empty review fields should never become fabricated ratings.

facts.fact: The page recommends changing a single meaningful element at a time in a review-layout test, such as the summary's position or the default sort, and defining the decision metric before launching.
facts.quote: Change a single meaningful element at a time, such as the summary’s position or the default sort, and define the decision metric before launching the experiment.

facts.fact: The page advises against stopping a review experiment early just because the early result matches the tester's preference.
facts.quote: Don’t stop an experiment just because the early result matches your preference.

facts.fact: The page states that its listed signal ranges are decision rules rather than universal performance thresholds.
facts.quote: Use these as decision rules, not universal performance thresholds.
